events.prompt: The broadcasters want a head-to-head. How do you play it?

choices.text: Accept and go on the attack
choices.resultText: You land blows and take a few. The overnight polls twitch your way.
A steady, on-message night. No gaffes, no fireworks.

choices.text: Decline: protect the lead, avoid the ambush
choices.resultText: You dodge the studio lights. The press calls it cowardice; your base calls it discipline.

events.headline: A Sunday tabloid is sitting on a story about {party}
events.prompt: A red-top has dirt. What's the play?

choices.text: Pre-but: get your version out first
choices.resultText: You blunt the splash. The story still runs, softer and on your terms.

choices.text: Ignore it and stay on message
choices.resultText: The splash dominates a news cycle. Your grid holds, barely.

choices.text: Threaten legal action and dare them
choices.resultText: They blink on the worst claims. You look thin-skinned to everyone else.

events.headline: {party}'s manifesto committee is split on the big pledge
events.prompt: The draft is ready. Which way do you push the manifesto?

choices.text: Go bold with a defining, risky pledge
choices.resultText: The base roars. The spreadsheets at HQ look nervous.

choices.text: Play it cautious: Ming vase politics
choices.resultText: No hostages to fortune. Also no spark.

choices.text: Make it a contrast document against the rival
choices.resultText: You define them more than yourself, and it lands.

events.headline: Activists beg {party} HQ for a late ground-game surge
events.prompt: Do you empty the war chest into the final ground push?

choices.resultText: Doors knocked, leaflets out. The machine is humming.

choices.text: Balanced: keep powder dry for broadcast
choices.resultText: A competent final week. Nothing wasted, nothing spectacular.

choices.text: Pivot to the air war instead
choices.resultText: The ads blanket the regions. Field organisers grumble.

1951.label: 1951 · Churchill v. Attlee
1951.tagline: October 1951. Six years of Labour austerity, rationing still on the shelves, and Churchill promising to set the people free. Can Attlee hold on, or does the old lion get one last roar?

1964.label: 1964 · Wilson v. Douglas-Home
1964.tagline: October 1964. Thirteen years of Conservative rule, a grouse-moor aristocrat against a Yorkshire technocrat, and the Profumo affair still hanging in the air. The narrowest of Labour wins.

1966.label: 1966 · Wilson v. Heath
1966.tagline: March 1966. A majority of four is no way to govern. Wilson goes back to the country to turn it into a mandate, and the white heat of technology carries Labour to a landslide.

1970.label: 1970 · Heath v. Wilson
1970.tagline: June 1970. Wilson is cruising, the polls call it for Labour, and then a bad set of trade figures and a heatwave weekend turn the whole thing over. Heath's upset nobody saw coming.

1979.label: 1979 · Thatcher v. Callaghan
1979.tagline: May 1979. The Winter of Discontent: strikes, the rubbish piled high, the dead unburied. A tired Labour government meets a new kind of Conservative. Labour isn't working.

1983.label: 1983 · Thatcher v. Foot
1983.tagline: June 1983. A Falklands triumph, mass unemployment, and a divided left: Labour's 'longest suicide note in history' against a rising Alliance. The landslide year.

1987.label: 1987 · Thatcher v. Kinnock
1987.tagline: June 1987. Boom in the South, bust in the North, and a slick Labour relaunch that still can't close the gap. Can Kinnock break the Thatcher grip?

1992.label: 1992 · Major v. Kinnock
1992.tagline: April 1992. A recession, a new Conservative leader, and Labour ahead in the polls. The election Labour was sure to win, and the shock that followed.

1997.label: 1997 · Blair v. Major
1997.tagline: May 1997. Eighteen years of Conservative rule, a tired government, and a rebranded opposition. Things can only get better. Can you finish the job?

2001.label: 2001 · Blair v. Hague
2001.tagline: June 2001. Four years of New Labour, a becalmed economy, and a Conservative Party still in the wilderness. The quiet landslide.

2005.label: 2005 · Blair v. Howard
2005.tagline: May 2005. Iraq hangs over a third Labour term, the Lib Dems surge on the anti-war vote, and Howard's Tories claw back. A majority, but a chastened one.

2010.label: 2010 · Brown v. Cameron v. Clegg
2010.tagline: May 2010. A banking crash, an expenses scandal, and the first TV debates of the age. 'I agree with Nick', and nobody wins outright.

2015.label: 2015 · Cameron v. Miliband
2015.tagline: May 2015. Five years of coalition, a UKIP surge, and an SNP tide rising in Scotland. The polls say a dead heat. They're about to be wrong.

2017.label: 2017 · May v. Corbyn
2017.tagline: June 2017. A snap election called from a commanding lead, but a manifesto wobble and a surging opposition turn a coronation into a knife-edge.

2019.label: 2019 · Johnson v. Corbyn
2019.tagline: December 2019. Three years of Brexit deadlock, a fractured opposition, and the Red Wall up for grabs. Break the impasse.

2024.label: 2024 · Starmer v. Sunak
2024.tagline: July 2024. Fourteen years of Tory government, a cost-of-living squeeze, and Reform eating the right. Labour smells a landslide. Don't fumble it.

1974feb.label: 1974 (Feb) · Heath v. Wilson
1974feb.tagline: February 1974. The miners are out, the lights go off three days a week, and Heath asks the country a straight question: who governs Britain? The answer is nobody, cleanly. A hung parliament.
1974feb.goalText: 318 of 635 seats (or the best hand in a hung parliament)

1974oct.label: 1974 (Oct) · Wilson v. Heath
1974oct.tagline: October 1974. Eight months of minority government, and Wilson goes back for the working majority he needs. He gets one of three, and it will melt away seat by seat.
